recs.push(`GOAL: settle the geometry-reduction argument that drives geometry_necessity for the curvature-field proposals, and re-check the algebra before using it as a counterexample.
READ: E12/E13/E14 of BRANCHCURV-SID and KAPPA_BRANCH (per-code kappa_k and per-pair harmonic-mean kbar_ik inside the Poincare assignment distance), and the ledger rows in E6.
OBSERVED: both proposals score codes with d_kappa(u,e_k)^2 (BRANCHCURV, divided by a frozen tau) or with the curvature-k bar distance plus a curvature-k commitment L_c = beta*d_kbar(p(r),p(c_{k*}))^2 (KAPPA_BRANCH).

When k varies only through the code index (BRANCHCURV) or through one fixed item and the code index (KAPPA_BRANCH), the "curvature field" is exactly a per-code gated Euclidean distance: no residual hyperbolic property (exponential volume growth, tree-likeness) survives, because that property needs one curvature shared by the whole candidate set. A matched Euclidean control (per-code weight/temperature on a Euclidean distance) reproduces the assignment exactly.
PLACED AT: BRANCHCURV-SID E12/E13/E14 and KAPPA_BRANCH E12/E13/E14, with the numeric band from the clamps (kappa_k in [0.25k0,4k0]; kbar in [1,2]).
OPEN: whether the softmax temperature tau (BRANCHCURV) adds anything a Euclidean temperature does not - it does not, so the reduction covers the soft-assignment version too.`);

PLACED AT: bundle bd8bbcbdc448cf32, items E2 E3 E5 E6 E8 E10 E12 E13 E14.
